2010_013_111610regmtg.paragraph: Agenda, prior minutes, the October 2010 Treasurer's Report and action backup for the Troy School District Board of Education regular meeting of November 16, 2010 at the Services Building, 4420 Livernois. The centerpiece is Assistant Superintendent Mark S. Rajter's updated five-year forecast, which without reductions carries the General Fund from revenue of $134,308,608 against expenditures of $135,793,505 in 2010/11 to $128,758,414 against $151,040,173 in 2013/14 and an ending fund balance of ($35,107,599); with proposed cuts of $6,000,000, $8,000,000 and $8,000,000 the 2013/14 balance instead ends at $6,892,401. Also on the agenda: a three-year water treatment award to Enerco Corporation at $80,365.00.

**Meeting and agenda**
Troy Board of Education, 7:00 PM, November 16, 2010, Services Building, 4420 Livernois, Troy, MI 48098 (district offices 4400 Livernois, 248.823.4000; www.troy.k12.mi.us). Meetings are cablecast on TS-TV Channel 19 (Comcast) and Channel 15 (WOW) every Monday and Wednesday at 2:00 and 9:00 p.m. except July and August. Item 3.A. proposes deleting Item 10.A., "Cancel December 7, 2010, Board of Education Meeting." Consent agenda items A-D: October 19, 2010 minutes; November 9, 2010 workshop minutes; Treasurer's Report - October, 2010; Bid Award - Water Treatment Chemicals. Curriculum item 7.A. is the Great Start Readiness Program, Business item 8.A. the Five-Year Forecast Presentation, and item 11.A. a closed session on attorney-client privilege and negotiations under the Michigan Open Meetings Act, Public Act 267, Section 8 (c).

**October 19, 2010 minutes**
President Underwood convened at 7:02 p.m. with Edmunds, Fleming, Hauff, Miletti and Philippart present and Pochodylo absent; Superintendent Fowler, administrators including Rajter and Machesky, 45 Martell Elementary students and about 65 other audience members attended. Martell fifth graders and teacher Mrs. Andrea Moon performed "Don't Let Drugs Get in the Way of Your Dreams," written for Red Ribbon Week under Troy Families for Safe Homes and the Troy Coalition. Resolution 10-107 honored 42 National Merit Scholarship Semifinalists; 10-108 approved the consent agenda; 10-109 approved new hire Jennifer Messacar; 10-110 accepted the audited 2010 financial statements presented by Teresa Pollock and Andrea Edwards of Plante & Moran; 10-111 adopted TYA by-laws changes. All carried 6 ayes, 0 nays, Pochodylo absent. Adjourned 8:45 p.m.; Nancy L. Philippart, Secretary. The November 9, 2010 workshop ran 6:04 p.m. to 10:32 p.m. (Miletti and Pochodylo absent).

**Water Treatment Bid #9695** - Bids opened October 19, 2010, sent to nine potential bidders with three responding. Enerco Corporation $20,835.00 / $29,630.00 / $29,900.00, total $80,365.00; H.V. Burton Co. $28,439.00 / $28,439.00 / $29,844.00, total $86,722.00; D & L Water Control $76,563.50 each year, total $229,690.50. Recommended by Mondo Belardi, Director of Maintenance, and Frank E. Lams, Supervisor of Purchasing and Budget.

**Great Start Readiness** - Resolution certifying participation for 2010-2011: no full-day preschool ($-0- at the $6,600 per-capita allowance), no parent involvement program ($-0-), and half-day preschool for 32 eligible four-year-olds funded at $108,800 on a $3,400 per-capita allowance under Sections 32d and 37 through 40 of the State School Aid Act.

**Five-year forecast** - Enrollment fell from 12,182 in 2007/2008 to 12,045 in 2010/2011. The district reports $39.3 million in reductions since 2002, a $20.4 million reduction in fund equity through 2009/2010, and $6.7 million cut for 2010-2011 (22.4 non-certified and 37.0 certified FTE). Assumptions hold the foundation allowance at $9,005, add a retirement increase of 20.8% (rate 20.66 to 25.0) and 12.0% annual health insurance growth.

**Identification.** Board of Education packet for the Troy School District regular meeting of November 16, 2010, 7:00 PM, Services Building, 4420 Livernois, Troy, Michigan 48098; district address 4400 Livernois, Troy, Michigan 48098, 248.823.4000, www.troy.k12.mi.us. Meetings are cablecast on TS-TV Channel 19 (Comcast) and Channel 15 (WOW) every Monday and Wednesday at 2:00 and 9:00 p.m. except July and August. Agenda: Pledge of Allegiance; Recognition; Additions and Deletions (Item 3.A. resolves that Item 10.A., "Cancel December 7, 2010, Board of Education Meeting," be deleted); Public Communication; Consent Agenda A-D (October 19, 2010 BOE minutes; November 9, 2010 Board Workshop minutes; Treasurer's Report - October, 2010; Bid Award - Water Treatment Chemicals); Personnel; Curriculum 7.A. Great Start Readiness Program; Business 8.A. Five-Year Forecast Presentation; Other 10.A.; Closed Session 11.A. Attorney-Client Privilege and Negotiations.

**Minutes of October 19, 2010.** President Underwood called the meeting to order at 7:02 p.m. Present: Edmunds, Fleming, Hauff, Miletti, Philippart and Underwood; Mrs. Pochodylo absent. Also present: Superintendent Fowler; administrators Birmingham, Keeling, Kwasny, Machesky, Mull, Papasian, Rajter, Seppanen and Witt; 45 students from Martell Elementary School and about 65 additional audience members. Mrs. Keeling introduced Martell fifth-grade winners of the 2009/2010 Red Ribbon Song Writing Contest, sponsored by Troy Families for Safe Homes and the Troy Coalition; with teacher Mrs. Andrea Moon they performed "Don't Let Drugs Get in the Way of Your Dreams," and Ms. Underwood and Mr. Miletti presented each child a certificate and pin. Ms. Emily Jambeau of Bemis Elementary announced a Fourth Grade Hit Song Contest with two winners to perform at the 2011 Festival of Songs Concert in January. Resolution 10-107 (Philippart/Edmunds) recognized 42 National Merit Scholarship Semifinalists who scored in the top one and one-half percent on the National Preliminary Scholastic Aptitude Test (PSAT). Resolution 10-108 (Edmunds/Miletti) approved the consent agenda: October 5, 2010 minutes, October 12, 2010 workshop minutes, Treasurer's Report - September, 2010, and Awarding of Bid for Copy Paper. Resolution 10-109 (Hauff/Fleming) approved new hire Jennifer Messacar. Rich Machesky and Mrs. Jennifer Taylor of Boulan Park Middle School presented APT to Succeed with TBERT, the Troy Business and Education Roundtable, begun by the Troy Chamber of Commerce and Larson Middle School; Troy High senior Lynsey Mukomel described her electronic portfolio. Resolution 10-110 (Fleming/Hauff) accepted the audited 2010 financial statements presented by Teresa Pollock and Andrea Edwards of Plante & Moran. Resolution 10-111 (Miletti/Philippart) adopted TYA by-laws changes. Each vote was 6 ayes, 0 nays, Pochodylo absent. Student representative Andrew Michail reported Rouge River water-quality work with nine tests contributed to Friends of the Rouge; Bria Ellis reported the Athens PTO's third Drive One Fundraiser raising $4,200 this year and $13,300 overall, a Red Cross Blood Drive November 10 from 8:00 a.m. to 2:00 p.m. with a goal of 76 pints requiring 113 donors, and Summuna, a Model UN conference October 23 with 20 schools and 520 delegates keynoted by State Senator Pappageorge. Mrs. Edmunds urged a yes vote on the November 2 election's Proposal 1 to keep the Troy Public Library open, which would otherwise close June 30. Adjourned 8:45 p.m.; Nancy L. Philippart, Secretary. The November 9, 2010 workshop ran 6:04 p.m. to 10:32 p.m. (Miletti and Pochodylo absent) on the Annual Cash Flow Projection Model, the Five-Year Forecast/Budget Update, a Shared Services Agreement and Board Policy Review.

**Bid Award #9695, Water Treatment Chemicals.** Memo of November 11, 2010 from Mondo Belardi, Director of Maintenance, to Frank Lams, Supervisor of Purchasing (Purchasing Department, 1140 Rankin St., Troy, MI 48083, 248/823-4050), and memo of November 9, 2010 from Frank E. Lams to Mark S. Rajter. Bids for heating and cooling system water treatment were opened October 19, 2010, sent to nine potential bidders with three responding, none a "No Bid." Enerco Corporation bid $20,835.00 for November 1, 2010 through June 30, 2011, $29,630.00 for 2011-12 and $29,900.00 for 2012-13, total $80,365.00; H.V. Burton Co. bid $28,439.00, $28,439.00 and $29,844.00, total $86,722.00; D & L Water Control bid $76,563.50 in each year, total $229,690.50. Enerco's tabulation prices E-2094 at $40.00 per gallon, E-2394 at $56.00, Stabrom-909 at $42.00, E-7334 at $56.00 and E-3284 at $38.00, with nine Dujector piston chemical pumps at $400, $420 and $450 each and monthly service calls and lab testing included in the purchase of chemicals. Award is recommended as an expenditure of the 2010-11, 2011-12 and 2012-13 General Fund.

**Great Start Readiness Grant Acceptance (Item 7.A.).** Resolution certifying participation in the 2010-2011 Great Start Readiness State Aid program under Sections 32d and 37 through 40 of the State School Aid Act. Under Section 38 the district is eligible for an allocation of $108,800 for fiscal year 2010-2011 to serve 32 children. The district will not provide full-day preschool ($-0- at the approved per-capita allowance of $6,600) and will not provide comprehensive parent involvement and education programs ($-0-), but will provide half-day preschool education for 32 eligible four-year-old children with $108,800 based on the approved per-capita allowance of $3,400; more than fifty percent of children enrolled will meet income eligibility guidelines, and unallocated funds are redistributed to other eligible districts. Adopted this 16th day of November 2010.

**Five-Year Forecast (Item 8.A.).** Presented by Mark S. Rajter; no action required. Enrollment history: 2005/2006 12,005; 2006/2007 12,129; 2007/2008 12,182; 2008/2009 12,165; 2009/2010 12,069; 2010/2011 12,045. Finances: $39.3 million in reductions since 2002; $20.4 million reduction in fund equity through 2009/2010; total reductions for 2010-2011 of $6.7 million; FTE reductions of 22.4 non-certified (administration, TESPA, TESA, non-represented) and 37.0 certified (TEA). Projections cite a 2011-12 revenue reduction of $6.2 million, with $270 per pupil equating to approximately $3.2 million and elimination of 20j costing $3.0 million annually. Revenue assumptions: foundation allowance remains at $9,005 per pupil in 2011-12 with no change for 2012-13 or 2013-14; no ARRA or Education Jobs federal funding; county special education revenue reduced $2.0 million through 2013-14 on declining property values. Expenditure assumptions: no salary increases beyond contractual step increases; retirement increase of 20.8% with the rate changing from 20.66 to 25.0; annual health insurance increases of 12.0%; enrollment per the VanDenBerghe study; 12 teacher retirements per year for the next three years.

**Remaining items.** Item 10.A. asks the Board to cancel the December 7, 2010 Board of Education Meeting, though Item 3.A. proposes deleting it from the agenda. Item 11.A. calls for a roll-call vote to enter closed session as permitted in the Michigan Open Meetings Act, Public Act 267, Section 8 (c), to discuss an attorney-client privilege item and negotiations, with Hauff, Miletti, Philippart, Pochodylo, Underwood, Edmunds and Fleming listed for the vote.
